edges.description: Enamel is thin to absent in both incisors and molars, and histology shows the ameloblast layer losing its palisade arrangement and laying down a thin disorganised matrix - the cellular counterpart of the human ultrastructural finding.
edges.limitations: A constitutive null, so it models complete loss whereas human alleles are hypomorphic; the mouse incisor grows continuously and is not a structural analogue of the human permanent tooth.

edges.description: The mouse has a skeletal phenotype, but the wrong one. It shows growth retardation, premature obliteration of the skull synchondroses, osteopetrosis of long bones and vertebrae, kyphosis and osteoarthritis - and specifically does not develop platyspondyly, the defining human finding.
edges.limitations: The direction of the bone phenotype is inverted relative to patients: the mouse is osteopetrotic through defective osteoclastic resorption, while affected humans have normal or reduced bone density. The murine axial skeleton is also mechanically unlike a bipedal spine, so the absence of platyspondyly may be a species difference in loading rather than in LTBP3 biology. Either way the model cannot be used as evidence about the human vertebral phenotype.

edges.description: The craniofacial half does translate: the mouse has a shortened skull base and disproportionately short upper jaw with the mandible extending beyond the maxilla, which is the same relative prognathism seen in patients.
edges.limitations: Restricted to the craniofacial skeleton, and the murine snout is not a structural analogue of the human midface, so the correspondence is at the level of relative jaw proportion rather than of shape.

nodes.description: Frameshift, nonsense and splice alleles predominate - a 14 bp deletion, a nonsense plus splice-donor compound heterozygote, and several single-base deletions, with missense alleles reported later. All are hypomorphic in effect rather than proven nulls, and all lie in or before the domains that do the TGF-beta binding.

nodes.description: The skeletal arm, and the weaker half of the model. Ltbp3 is expressed in cartilage primordia including the developing vertebrae, and TGF-beta is the most abundant growth factor in bone with an established role in endochondral ossification; deregulating it is expected to disturb axial patterning. What is missing is a demonstration in this disease: the knockout mouse, which is otherwise a good model, does not develop platyspondyly.

nodes.description: LTBP3 is one of four LTBP/fibrillin-family proteins. Through its eight-cysteine TB domains it forms a large complex with latent TGF-beta 1, 2 and 3, and it is this complex that anchors the growth factor in the extracellular matrix where it can later be activated. The functional consequence of removing LTBP3 is therefore not loss of a structural fibre but loss of a reservoir: less TGF-beta is positioned for release, so less signalling reaches the cells that need it.

nodes.description: The tissue-level result: enamel that is thin, irregular and in places absent. Clinically the teeth are small, yellow and widely spaced with large pulp chambers and taurodontic molars, and because the protective layer is missing they are prone to infection and early loss. The founding family's dentine was normal, and that observation is load-bearing for the ameloblast-specific reading of the mechanism - but it does not generalise: a later family had abnormal dentine and calcified dental pulp blood vessels, curated below as a REFUTE item rather than set aside.

nodes.description: Ltbp3 is transcribed by differentiating ameloblasts and odontoblasts, with transcripts at the apical secretory pole of the ameloblast - the end of the cell that builds enamel. The ultrastructural phenotype in patients points at a specific step: the initial aprismatic layer at the dentine-enamel junction is absent, a thin irregular prismatic shell is laid down instead, and non-prismatic enamel then appears in patches on top. That pattern implicates the formation and modulation of Tomes' process, the secretory specialisation that determines prism architecture, rather than a general failure to secrete matrix. Dentine was normal on ultrastructural examination in the founding family, which is what makes the defect ameloblast-specific rather than a mineralisation defect of the whole tooth - but abnormal dentine has since been reported in a later family, so that specificity is not absolute.

nodes.description: The mainstay of care, and the only thing that alters day-to-day life in this disease. Unprotected dentine is painful and hypersensitive and the teeth break down quickly, so restoration is done early and for symptom control as much as for appearance. Note the evidence base: it comes from non-syndromic amelogenesis imperfecta, because no series reports restorative outcomes in LTBP3-related disease specifically. The enamel phenotype is the same lesion, which is the argument for importing it, and every item here is graded INDIRECT to say that the argument is an inference and not a result in this disease.
